lede: The biggest thing happening this week in local government is a Tuesday public hearing at Telluride Town Council on a vesting period extension for a development project — that's a vote worth showing up for. The same morning, Council takes up the Flock Safety automated license plate reader system, a privacy-versus-public-safety conversation that rarely stays quiet for long. Meanwhile, both San Miguel County and Mountain Village are deep in 2027 budget season, and a Wednesday BOCC session includes public hearings on affordable housing fee waivers in the Ilium Valley and a joint Planning Commission work session on affordable housing code updates.

notable.stake: Public hearing on development vesting extension; ALPR camera privacy debate with public input.
Public hearings on affordable housing fee waivers and a lot line adjustment affecting county land use.
Joint BOCC-Planning Commission work session actively shaping county affordable housing code policy.
Vote on mortgage exception for deed-restricted homeowner — sets precedent for housing rules.
